Sources and credits

LexiMaster has 43,273 entries. Your study progress is stored only in this browser; nothing is sent to a server.

Definitions, pronunciations and word origins

Dictionary definitions, IPA transcriptions, synonyms, antonyms and etymologies come from Wiktionary, by its contributors, under the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 license. They were selected, re-ordered, shortened and converted to American spelling for this app; that adapted material is shared under the same license. Some entries came from the Free Dictionary API, which is also built on Wiktionary.

Short definitions of related words that have no entry of their own (a synonym, antonym or compared word you tap), and the related forms under Word forms, come from Open English WordNet 2025, by the Global WordNet Association and its contributors, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license; it builds on Princeton WordNet, WordNet 3.1 Copyright 2011 by Princeton University (license). Tenses, plurals and comparatives come from LemmInflect (MIT license), built on the SPECIALIST Lexicon of the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

American IPA for words without a Wiktionary transcription was converted from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary, Copyright © 1993–2015 Carnegie Mellon University (license).

How to say it

The mouth drawings were made for LexiMaster. The real-mouth clips are short, trimmed, evenly lit excerpts of speaker sub009 from the USC 75-Speaker Speech MRI Database (Lim et al., 2021, Scientific Data 8:187), by the Signal Analysis and Interpretation Laboratory of the University of Southern California, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 license; the tongue and teeth outlines on them were added for LexiMaster.

Example sentences, meanings and study notes

Conversation examples, meanings for expressions that dictionaries don't list, the AI senses and the study notes (usage notes, distinctions, collocations, pronunciation tips) were written for LexiMaster, with the help of Claude by Anthropic.

Software and fonts

sql.js (SQLite in WebAssembly), MIT license (license). Fonts: Literata, IBM Plex Sans and Charis SIL, under the SIL Open Font License 1.1 (Literata, IBM Plex Sans, Charis SIL).

Recorded pronunciations

24,792 American English recordings from Wikimedia Commons, by the volunteers below, under the licenses shown. Each was converted from its original format to AAC (.m4a). Open a name to see the words; each word links to its recording's page, with the full author and license details.

Vealhurl · 8,728 recordings · CC BY-SA 4.0

Synthesized pronunciations

The 18,481 entries without an American recording have a natural synthesized one, made for LexiMaster with Kokoro (the Kokoro-82M model by hexgrad, Apache License 2.0), voice “Heart”, through kokoro-onnx (MIT license). Rare words and names are spoken from each entry's reviewed American IPA; common words and everyday phrases are read by the model directly.
